answer: Each agent runs a glacier-slow sequential hash chain keyed to the network beacon, where each epoch's seed forces recomputation from the previous checkpoint; sybils cannot parallelize because the bridge between epochs requires the prior output as input, so forging N identities costs N times the wall-clock duration of a full epoch — an attacker spinning up 10,000 fake nodes still waits the same months per identity, burning electricity with no speedup.
